key_insight: Encoder–decoder operator learning can be analyzed in a resolution-independent way by passing to a limiting kernel, so learning bounds no longer depend on a specific input/output discretization.
engineering_relevance: This gives practical error and complexity guarantees for neural operator models built from finite-resolution encodings such as Fourier, wavelets, PCA, sampling, and wide encoder–decoder networks.
method: Construct matrix-valued kernels on encoded spaces and lift them to operator-valued kernels on the original function spaces.
Prove operator-norm convergence of induced kernels to a limiting kernel as resolution increases.
Derive regularized SGD and NTK error bounds that separate encoding, optimization, and finite-width effects.
evidence_signal: The paper provides upper and lower theoretical error bounds, showing that the encoding-induced terms are both quantifiable and generally unavoidable under the analyzed assumptions.
watch_item: The guarantees rely on asymptotic kernel convergence and decay assumptions, so performance may degrade if the chosen encoding does not resolve the target operator well.
paper_title: Resolution-Independent Analysis of Encoder--Decoder Operator Learning via Limiting Kernels
